sources.entry: markupsafe - Safely adds untrusted strings to HTML/XML markup.

summary.one_liner: MarkupSafe is a Python library providing a Markup text type that escapes special characters so untrusted strings can be safely placed in HTML and XML.
summary.what_it_does: MarkupSafe implements a str-subclass called Markup that escapes characters with special meaning in HTML and XML. The escape() function replaces characters such as angle brackets so they display as text rather than being interpreted as markup. Wrapping a string in Markup marks it as already safe, so it is not escaped again. Methods and operators on Markup, such as format(), escape their arguments automatically. The README's examples show escaping a script tag and escaping a quoted value passed into a template string. The README is short and does not describe a broader feature set.
use_cases: escaping untrusted user input before rendering HTML
preventing cross-site scripting in Python web templates
marking trusted HTML fragments as safe
safely formatting HTML strings with placeholders
notable: Markup is a str subclass whose methods and operators escape their arguments
escape() wraps the result in Markup so it is not escaped twice
caveats: The README gives no installation instructions or list of supported Python versions
The README does not describe how it integrates with specific template engines
